justifications.research.methodologyDepth: K awards require a structured didactic plan in study design, biostatistics, and (for K23) clinical/patient-oriented methods, typically delivered via CTSA or KL2 coursework.
justifications.research.publicationTrack: K awardees publish at substantially higher rates than non-K early-career peers, with median 10-20 peer-reviewed papers during the award period.
justifications.research.grantReadiness: The explicit purpose of K awards is preparing recipients to win R01/R-series funding, with grant-writing built into the career development plan.
justifications.research.pathwayToIndependence: K-to-R transition is the canonical NIH pipeline to PI status; ~30-40% of K23 holders secure R01 within a decade, the highest rate of any rehab-research credential.
justifications.research.interdisciplinaryFit: Mentorship teams typically span clinical medicine, biostatistics, engineering, and public health, and K12/KL2 programs explicitly foster cross-disciplinary collaboration.
justifications.research.efficiency: 3-5 years of 75%-protected effort post-PhD/postdoc with ~25-30% funding rates makes this one of the most time- and cost-intensive credentials in rehab science.
